title: Structs: Custom Data Types
description: Create your own data types by grouping related data together. Learn to define, initialize, and use structs effectively.

sections.title: What are Structs?
Struct Syntax Comparison
sections.explanation: BPL struct syntax uses field: type format with commas between fields. Very similar to Rust.

sections.title: Defining and Using Structs
sections.expectedOutput:
Name: Alice
Age: 30
Height: 1.65 m

Bob is 25 years old

lineExplanations.19: Access fields with the dot operator: variable.field.
lineExplanations.4-8: Define the struct with its fields. Each field has name: type.
lineExplanations.12-16: Create an instance with struct literal: TypeName { field: value, ... }.

sections.title: Modifying Struct Fields
sections.expectedOutput:
Click Counter: 0
After increment: 1
After adding 10: 11
Updated Counter: 11

lineExplanations.17: Modify fields using assignment: struct.field = newValue.
lineExplanations.24: You can change any field, including strings.

sections.title: Nested Structs
sections.expectedOutput:
Rectangle:
  Position: (10, 20)
  Size: 100 x 50
  Area: 5000
  Moved to: (50, 20)

lineExplanations.23: Chain the dot operator: rect.topLeft.x accesses nested field.
lineExplanations.8-12: Structs can contain other structs as fields.

sections.title: Passing Structs to Functions
sections.expectedOutput:
p1: Point(0, 0)
p2: Point(3, 4)
Distance: 7
p1 after move: Point(5, 10)

lineExplanations.9: Passing struct by value creates a copy.
lineExplanations.14: *Point means pointer to Point - can modify the original.

sections.title: Arrays of Structs
sections.expectedOutput:
Class Roster:
  Alice: 92

lineExplanations.14: Array of structs - each element is a full Student.
lineExplanations.24: Access array element, then its field: students[i].name.
lineExplanations.30: Compare fields of different array elements.

sections.title: Struct Best Practices
sections.content:
✅ **Group related data** - If variables always go together, make a struct

✅ **Use meaningful names** - `Point` not `P`, `Rectangle` not `Rect`

✅ **Keep structs focused** - Each struct should represent one concept

✅ **Pass large structs by pointer** - Avoid copying big structs

✅ **Initialize all fields** - Don't leave fields uninitialized

✅ **Consider methods** - We'll learn about struct methods next!

sections.title: Practice: Book Library
sections.instructions:
Create a Book struct with: title (string), author (string), year (int), pages (int).
Then:
1. Create an array of 3 books
2. Print all books
3. Find and print the oldest book
sections.hint: Use a loop to find the book with the smallest year value.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.content:
✅ **struct** creates a custom data type with named fields

✅ **Fields** are defined as `name: type` separated by commas

✅ **Initialize** with: `TypeName { field: value, ... }`

✅ **Access fields** with the dot operator: `instance.field`

✅ **Nested structs** - structs can contain other structs

✅ **Pass by pointer** (`*StructName`) to modify the original

✅ **Arrays of structs** work like arrays of any other type
